But ye shall receive power — and shall be witnesses to me - That is, ye shall be empowered to witness my Gospel, both by your preaching and suffering.

glossa.text: *I made a discourse.* That is, I wrote: because to write is to work. Or he says it thus, because by his deeds he deserved to be the writer of the Gospel. *I made.* The whole book of the Gospel is called one discourse, in that it has one sense: or the singular stands for the plural. The Gospel is a good announcement, by which is announced rest after labour, a kingdom after servitude, life after death. *Of all things.* Of the sayings and deeds of Christ which he judged worthy of his office or fit for his dispensation. *O Theophilus.* Theophilus is the same as friend of God, or lover of God: and if thou art a friend of God, it is written for thee. *Which Jesus began to do.* From the baptism of John by which Jesus was baptized, *until the day* on which he was taken up into heaven: because Luke wove the discourses concerning that whole time, who at the end of the Gospel wrote thus: *When he had blessed, he departed from them and was carried into heaven. To do.* He appoints or instructs a good teacher, one who does what he teaches.

*Giving commandment to the apostles* to preach the Gospel *through the Holy Spirit,* through whom the Gospel was preached, because he inspired the words and bestowed confidence. Or, *giving commandment through the Holy Spirit,* that is, what the Son commands, this the Holy Spirit also commands. Or, he gave the commandment on account of the Spirit, because he would not command unless the Spirit were about to come. *He chose.* This turns to the praise of the apostles, whose acts he purposes to write. *Taken up.* Taken up by the Divinity, or by a cloud, as true man.

*Alive.* A living and proper body, not a phantasmal one, which the apostles also recognized as most well known. Or alive, in that after death he was living. Or alive, that is, no more to die. *Through days.* Yet he did not appear to them through forty continuous days: for John says that after the day of the resurrection four other days intervened. After which he appeared again through forty: because he had been dead for forty hours, for forty days he confirms that he lives. And by the forty a type of the present age may be understood, in which Christ is engaged in the Church: or because man, consisting of four elements, is instructed against the transgression of the Decalogue.

*Eating together with them.* He announces the signs of a true body, because not by one sense of the body, but by sight, by hearing, by touch, by appearing, by speaking, by eating together, he proved that he had risen. *The promise,* which he promised through Joel, as is had in what follows: and if it was made by Christ, yet it will be fulfilled by the Father. Or it is called *of the Father,* because it is promised in his Word, that is, in Christ.

*For John. ((BEDA.))* When the Lord said: For John baptized with water, but you, etc., *as far as* that which was not done in the baptism of John.

Baptism is given in two natures, namely the bodily and the spiritual: because the man who is baptized consists of two: namely of body and of soul, yet baptism is one, as the man is one.

*But you,* etc. When Peter denied, the apostles were not baptized; not with water, but with the spirit: for after the resurrection it was said: *But you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit.* For they had not yet been confirmed by the resurrection of Christ and by the mission of the Spirit. But as circumcision was not necessary to the just before it was commanded to Abraham and to his posterity: so after the sacrament of the New Testament, that is baptism, was given in the place of circumcision by the Lord saying: *Unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Spirit ((Joan. III))*, etc., it is certain that none belongs to the body of Christ save the baptized, apart from those to whom the passion is reckoned in place of baptism. Likewise it is written when Paul was baptized: and it is not written when the other apostles were baptized: but we ought to understand that they were baptized on account of that: *Unless a man be born again,* etc.

*It is not for you to know.* He does not say, it will not be, but *it is not:* noting that they are still weak, and therefore not fit for the knowing of the secret: but when he says: *It is not for you to know,* he shows that he himself knows, whose are all things that are the Father's, but that it is not expedient for them to know, but that they should so live as though they were to be judged daily. *Which the Father.* The time of that kingdom, he says, is so secret that it lies open only to the knowledge of the Father, *but you shall receive the power of the Holy Spirit,* that what through the weakness of the flesh you cannot do, you may be able to do out of the power of the Holy Spirit. *In his own power.* This he said excusably as true man, but there is only one power of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit: the Son also is the power of the Father.

*But you shall receive.* The knowledge of the times is taken away, but the divine help of which they stand in need is applied: in this manner, when something is taken from children, another thing is given lest they be utterly saddened. *Of the Holy Spirit coming upon you.* When the Spirit shall come upon you, he will not bring the kingdom of Israel, or the kingdom of God in Israel, as you think, but he will bestow upon you the power of bearing witness of me, and the time of that kingdom is so far off, that first the fame of the Gospel shall run through not only Jerusalem, but all the borders of Judaea and of Samaria, and even the bounds of the world round about. *In Jerusalem and in all Judaea.* The consequence of order is preserved in the names of the places: to Jerusalem succeeds the nearest province of Judaea, to which Samaria is joined by situation, and thereafter the fellowship of the whole earth is brought in. *In Jerusalem.* Mystically: in the vision of peace, in the confession of the true faith: in the keeping of the commandments of God: and he foretold that they would preach among those who shall have made themselves strangers from the earth, through whom, as through the spokes of a wheel, from the middle of the earth where he wrought salvation, spiritual grace and saving doctrine flowed out through the whole world.

*And when he had said these things.* Mark records it otherwise, saying: *And the Lord Jesus indeed, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven ((Matth. XXVIII))*. But because Luke added more significantly: *When he had said these things, he was lifted up,* he shows that, those discourses being finished which he had recorded, the Lord ascended the heavens.

*Galilaeans, why stand you looking up to heaven?* In whom there ought to be a more prudent understanding, because the Galilaeans excelled the rest of the Jews in wisdom. Or, Galilaeans, the changeable, because by the instability of their sense they will have forgotten the commandments of God.

notes.text: Subdue — He speaks this in the name of the whole church, to which all particular believers were to submit themselves in the Lord.

Chuse — He will appoint and bestow upon us. Inheritance - The presence and worship, and blessing of God. This God had chosen for the Israelites and resolved to chuse or set apart for the Gentiles. Of Jacob - Of the people of Jacob or Israel, who are frequently called Jacob, for these did actually enjoy the presence of God in his sanctuary. Loved - Not for any peculiar worth in them, but for his free love to them, as he declareth, Deut. vii, 7, 8.

God — This is meant literally of the ark: but mystically of Christ's ascension into heaven, as may be gathered by comparing this with Eph. iv, 8, where the like words uttered concerning the ark upon the same occasion, chap. lxviii, 18, are directly applied to Christ's ascension.

The king — Not only ours, but of all the nations of the world. Sing - Not formally and carelessly, but seriously, considering the greatness of this king whom you praise, and what abundant cause you have to praise him.

The throne — Heaven is often called God's throne, whence God is said to behold and to rule all nations; of which general dominion of God, he here speaks. And Christ sits at his father's right-hand, for that purpose.

The princes — The Gentiles, who were divided in their principles, and interests, and religions, are now united and gathered together to Christ, laying their scepters at his feet, and jointly owning his worship and service. And altho' he mentions their conversion only, yet the conversion of their people might reasonably be supposed. Of the God - He doth not say the people of Abraham, lest this should be appropriated to the Israelites; but the people of the God of Abraham who worship the God of Abraham, whether they be Jews or Gentiles. The Shields - The princes or rulers, who are called shields, Hosea iv, 18, because by their office they are the common prosecutors of all their people. These are the Lord's, at his disposal, or subject to his dominion, both as to their hearts and kingdoms. Exalted - By this means God shall be greatly glorified. The glory and excellency of the church, ver. 1-3. Which God preserves from her enemies, ver. 4-8. God is praised for this, ver. 9, 10. Who effectually provides for its safety, ver. 11-14 A song and psalm for the sons of Korah.

glossa.text: *All ye Gentiles.* ((AUG.)) As if he should say: they insult, the boys, saying: *Bald head, bald head,* you, all the Gentiles to whom grace has passed over: *Clap your hands,* etc. The Gentiles to whom grace has passed over, and whom in the former psalm he called to faith, he invites to praise.
*High.* ((HIER.)) Powerful in what he wills. *Terrible.* ((REMIG.)) Because he is to judge in power.

*He hath subdued the peoples unto us.* ((CASS.)) This befits faithful men, to whom all outsiders are made subject, or, he has subjected to himself those who are to be associated with us. *The peoples,* the Jews. *Unto us. ((Ibid.))* Namely to the universal Church; this it befits all the faithful to say, to whom outsiders are made subject. *Under the feet. ((Ibid.))* By *feet,* understand preachers, to whom the peoples are made subject. ((AUG.)) *Under the feet.* So is the Church exalted, that it has those not yet believing under its feet.

*He hath chosen for us,* etc. Or in the person of the Apostles, he chose to give us his inheritance, of many peoples, that we may cultivate it, striking their hearts with the sword of preaching, and destroying their malice. *The inheritance.* ((AUG.)) The heavenly inheritance is the beauty of the Christian people, in which he shall be comely, shining as the sun, who now is abject. *The beauty of Jacob which,* etc. That is, those like to Jacob or signed by Jacob, who give earthly things for heavenly, as Jacob did, which was the grace of God, because *he loved him, Esau being reprobate.*

*He is ascended.* ((CASS.)) Diapsalma, the ascension and the kingdom of God is described, whence he urgently admonishes to sing psalms. *In jubilation.* ((AUG.)) The joy of the wondering Apostles, etc., *as far as* what can neither be kept silent nor be uttered.
*Sing ye psalms.* ((CASS.)) Praise by works: very salutary is that which is so often repeated, because it is God who creates, and a king governing the things created.

*Of all the earth. ((Ibid.))* Not as Jupiter of Crete, Mars of Thrace. *Wisely.* He teaches how one ought to sing psalms. Of old they sang psalms without understanding, while they worshipped stones. ((AUG.)) No one does wisely what he does not understand.
*He shall reign. ((Ibid.))* Now is this prophecy fulfilled: *God sitteth upon the holy seat. The holy seat.* ((AUG.)) Thrones, Virtues, and the saints.

*The princes of the peoples.* ((CASS.)) The first-fruits of all the Gentiles came together by believing in Christ, because, the Jews being cast out, the Gentiles succeed into the sons of Abraham, having the promise, because the Jews were lifted up in pride. ((HIER., CASS.)) Or *the strong gods,* namely the Apostles, whom neither death nor life shall separate from the charity of Christ. *Lifted up,* by miracles and doctrine.

notes.text: Since I heard of your faith and love — That is, of their perseverance and increase therein.
I cease not — In all my solemn addresses to God. To give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers - So he did of all the churches, Col. i, 9.

That the Father of that infinite glory which shines in the face of Christ, from whom also we receive the glorious inheritance, ver. 18, may give you the Spirit of wisdom and Revelation — The same who is the Spirit of promise is also, in the progress of the faithful, the Spirit of wisdom and Revelation; making them wise unto salvation, and revealing to them the deep things of God. He is here speaking of that wisdom and Revelation which are common to all real Christians.

The eyes of your understanding — It is with these alone that we discern the things of God. Being first opened, and then enlightened - By his Spirit. That ye may know what is the hope of his calling - That ye may experimentally and delightfully know what are the blessings which God has called you to hope for by his word and his Spirit. And what is the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints - What an immense treasure of blessedness he hath provided as an inheritance for holy souls.

And what the exceeding greatness of his power toward us who believe — Both in quickening our dead souls, and preserving them in spiritual life. According to the power which he exerted in Christ, raising him from the dead - By the very same almighty power whereby he raised Christ; for no less would suffice.

And he hath seated him at his own right hand — That is, he hath exalted him in his human nature, as a recompence for his sufferings, to a quiet, everlasting possession of all possible blessedness, majesty, and glory.

Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion — That is, God hath invested him with uncontrollable authority over all demons in hell, all angels in heaven, and all the princes and potentates on earth. And every name that is named - We know the king is above all, though we cannot name all the officers of his court. So we know that Christ is above all, though we are not able to name all his subjects. Not only in this world, but also in that which is to come - The world to come is so styled, not because it does not yet exist, but because it is not yet visible. Principalities and powers are named now; but those also who are not even named in this world, but shall be revealed in the world to come, are all subject to Christ.

And he hath given him to be head over all things to the church — An head both of guidance and government, and likewise of life and influence, to the whole and every member of it. All these stand in the nearest union with him, and have as continual and effectual a communication of activity, growth, and strength from him, as the natural body from its head.

The fulness of him that filleth all in all — It is hard to say in what sense this can be spoken of the church; but the sense is easy and natural, if we refer it to Christ, who is the fulness of the Father.

glossa.text: *Therefore.* The benefits conferred upon the human race, or upon the apostles, or upon the Ephesians having been enumerated, the Apostle subjoins what he thinks concerning their benefits, namely that he gives thanks, and asks that more be added, lest they be proud, but stretch beyond.
*That God,* etc. As if he should say: to obtain it I put forward not merits, but that he is God and the Father of Christ, etc.

*The eyes of the heart.* In his own image, therefore, know thou its author, who is not attained by bodily sense. Do not, therefore, think that God is attained by bodily sense, but with the eyes of the mind hear him. In the body, where the members are diverse, thou hearest in one place, thou seest in another. But in thy heart, where diverse members are not found, there thou hearest where thou seest. And to this end may he enlighten the eyes. *That you may know,* etc. This he says that they may be the more inclined: because when they shall fully know what the fruit of believers is, they will become the more inclined toward the cultivating of religion. Or thus: that hope be taken properly. And the sense is: That you may know what it is, namely his will *voluntas*; read *vocatio*, "calling", that is, how much the hope of eternal life avails, unto which he calls. And that you may know what the fulfilment of that hope is. Which he thus says: *And what are the riches.* Here he discloses what he understood by the name of hope: for he takes hope as the thing hoped for.

*What is the exceeding greatness.* The highest doctors shall have a certain increase of glory, beyond that which all shall have in common. For all shall have the same penny. *But star differeth from star in brightness ((I Cor. XV))*. *And there shall be diverse mansions in the house of the Father ((Joan. XIV))*.

*Raising him up,* etc. Now the example of the glory of the saints consists in the resurrection of the Saviour, that in it the faithful may know what has been promised to them. *At his right hand.* The right hand is the eternal beatitude which is given to the saints: the left is the misery which is given to the wicked. For by no form of body is God bounded and enclosed.

*Above every,* etc. This he says on account of the incarnation of the Son of God, that even having been made man he may be said to be above all the heavens, and above every creature, having his name by nature, not by adoption.

*Under his feet,* etc. By the feet full subjection is noted, and all things are deservedly subject to him, because they were made through him; or, the feet signify the humanity, because as the foot is the lower part of the body, so in Christ the lower nature is the humanity, which even the angels adore. *And him,* etc. After he has commemorated the dignity of Christ, he returns to us, showing that his dignity pertains to us; as if he should say: God so exalted Christ that this his exaltation pertains to us: because he himself is the head, and we the body, that we may partake of him. *The head.* According to the deity: because all were made by him, and also according to the humanity, by which the Church is joined to him, by nature and by grace. *For of his fullness we have all received ((Joan. X))*.

*His fullness.* Because he is filled up through them, yet being all things in all, here and in the time to come. Likewise. When those who have entered unto confession bend the knee to Christ, he is filled up, because those who withdraw seem to empty him. *All things in all.* Because the members confer nothing upon him, but he himself all things upon the members: because by his power they are what they are.

notes.text: And he said — On the day of his ascension. In the law, and the prophets, and the Psalms - The prophecies as well as types, relating to the Messiah, are contained either in the books of Moses (usually called the law) in the Psalms, or in the writings of the prophets; little being said directly concerning him in the historical books.

Then opened he their understanding, to understand the Scriptures — He had explained them before to the two as they went to Emmaus. But still they understood them not, till he took off the veil from their hearts, by the illumination of his Spirit.

Beginning at Jerusalem — This was appointed most graciously and wisely: graciously, as it encouraged the, greatest sinners to repent, when they saw that even the murderers of Christ were not excepted from mercy: and wisely, as hereby Christianity was more abundantly attested; the facts being published first on the very spot where they happened.
Behold I send the promise — Emphatically so called; the Holy Ghost.
He led them out as far as Bethany — Not the town, but the district: to the Mount of Olives, Acts i, 12, which stood within the boundaries of Bethany.

And while he was blessing them, he was parted from them — It was much more proper that our Lord should ascend into heaven, than that he should rise from the dead, in the sight of the apostles. For his resurrection was proved when they saw him alive after his passion: but they could not see him in heaven while they continued on earth. Please see Notes at Matt. i, 1

glossa.text: *Then he opened.* After the sight, after the touch, after the law recalled to mind, he opened their understanding, that they might understand what they see and read; then, after the truth of his own body had been commended, he commends the unity of the Church: *And that there should be preached in his name.*

*It behoved,* etc. It behoved that the ministers who were to preach penance and remission unto all nations should begin from Jerusalem. Not only because to them were entrusted the oracles of God, and because theirs is the adoption of sons, and the glory the testaments, and the law-giving; but for this reason also, that the Gentiles, entangled in various errors and crimes, might by this token above all of the divine loving-kindness be roused to the hope of pardon: that he grants pardon to those who crucified the Son of God.

*But stay you.* After he had perfectly instructed the disciples about the power of preaching, although he could of a sudden, if he willed, have strengthened them, he put it off, saying: *But stay you.* That he might give an example to those who follow, lest the imperfect presume to preach before the time. He sits in the city who binds himself within the cloisters of the mind, lest by speaking he wander abroad outside; so that when he has been perfectly clothed with the divine power, then he may go forth as it were out of himself, by instructing others.

*And he led them out.* Passing over all that was done through the forty days, he silently joins to the first day of the resurrection the last, on which he ascended into heaven. And beautifully, being about to bless the disciples, he leads them out to Bethany, which is called the house of obedience: because he who came down on account of the disobedience of the perverse, ascended on account of the obedience of the converted.

*In the temple.* That in the place of prayer, amid the devotions of praise, with hearts made ready in all things, they might await the promised coming of the Holy Spirit. So let us, after the solemnities of the passion and the resurrection have been celebrated in Jerusalem, that is, in the vision of peace, seek Bethany with the Lord for our leader, that with a quiet mind we may be steeped in the sacraments of his body and blood, and may take care to be a house of obedience.

*Praising and blessing.* Luke, who took upon himself to set forth Christ's priesthood more fully than the rest, and therefore began his Gospel from the ministry of the temple through the priesthood of Zachary, beautifully completed it in the devotion of the temple, when he concludes with the apostles there, ministers, namely, of the new priesthood to come, not in the blood of victims, but in the praise of God and in blessing.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Clap your hands, all you peoples.
God has gone up with a shout!
While he blessed them, he was lifted up.
And a cloud took him from their sight.
Why do you stand looking into heaven?
He will come in the same way.
Sing praises to our God and King. Come, let us worship.
Jesus is Lord of all!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Lift your eyes with the disciples on the hill, watching his hands rise over you in blessing one last time.
God has gone up with a shout!
A cloud receives him, and the sky seems suddenly empty, and two strangers ask why you keep staring up.
God has gone up with a shout!
But he is not gone; he is enthroned, head over all things, filling everything in every way.
God has gone up with a shout!
So sound the trumpet, clap your hands, and sing: the one who walked our roads now reigns.
God has gone up with a shout! Jesus is Lord!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: He lifted his hands and blessed them.
God has gone up with a shout!
A cloud took him; the sky stood open.
God has gone up with a shout!
He reigns now, head over all things.
God has gone up with a shout!
Come, let us worship the ascended Lord.
Jesus is Lord of all!
